name: The Fate of Tlemcen
outcome: Tlemcen made a fiefdom of Morocco
note: Morocco's war, begun two years before the campaign. Granada answered Morocco's call three days before it ended, and lost no one.

name: The Moroccan War on Castile
outcome: Defeat for Morocco: it gives up all its land on the Iberian side of the Strait (Trent's account).
note: Tunis and its vassals (Tripoli, Gabès, Gafsa, Touggourt, Bijaya) joined Morocco on 9 November 1338. Castile won the first five battles; Morocco took the sixth at Shalūqa in June 1339, and Tlemcen held al-Karash in August. Morocco's side holds Ishbīliyya and the whole Murcia area (Mursiyya, Siyāsa, Qarṭājanna, Lawraqa, Mūla); Trent's account has Tunisian troops taking Murcia. Granada can still be called in and has not been.

name: The War on Aragon
goal: Reclaim Andalusia (Granada's casus belli against Aragon)
outcome: Victory: Aragon cedes thirteen locations south of Castellón and Teruel, from Balansiyya and Shāṭiba to Uryūla and Jumalla, and pays war reparations for ten years
note: Declared on 24 May 1339 (confirmed by the save). Majorca, Navarre and Cagliari joined Aragon at once. Morocco and Tunis can be called in and have not been. The first fighting was a skirmish at Jumalla in August; on 8 November Ibn al-Khaṭīb won a great victory at Uryūla (Orihuela), worth 25 war score (Trent's screenshots), and laid siege to the town. Uryūla fell on 30 May 1340, as Castile laid siege to Mursiyya and cut the road home (Trent's account). Peace was made on 11 August 1340. Trent's account: with Aragon's field army down to some 6,000 against our 16,000, and our own supply in doubt, the sultan threatened to march on Barcelona; Aragon conceded everything south of Castellón de la Plana and Teruel, with a large indemnity.

name: The Second Moroccan War on Castile
note: Six years after its defeat of 1340, Morocco declares war again under the game's scripted Marinid casus belli to reclaim al-Andalus. Castile's alliances bring in Portugal and Aragon, with Majorca and Cagliari, so all three crowns of Iberia stand together. Tafilalt, Touat and Tlemcen march with Morocco at once; Tunis and its marches (Tripoli, Gabès, Gafsa, Bijaya and the Sahel) join on 18 October. Granada, Castile's tributary and alone on the Iberian shore, answered the call on 18 October and brought the Ṭāʾifa of Balansiyya with it; going to war with its overlord ended the tributary bond. The Volunteers of the Faith rose again under Yaḥyā Raḥḥū (saves of 18 October and 8 November 1346; Trent's account). Tripoli, Gafsa and the Sahel had left Morocco's side by July 1348. Portugal made a separate peace on 2 September 1348, annulling its treaties with Castile for ten years and paying reparations (Trent's screenshot). On 27 January 1349 Castile, broken by the plague, made a separate peace with Granada alone, the Peace of Qurṭuba: Granada took 23 locations from Qurṭuba and Ishbīliyya to Jayyān, the Ṭāʾifa of Mursiyya took the Murcia area, Castile paid reparations and annulled its treaties with Aragon, and Granada returned to the name of Castile's tributary. Morocco fights on.
